label: PF Backlog 574
title: Defect/RCCA: assignment lease not coordinated across sessions -> double-claim (two sessions claim the same item); PF must be a SINGLE shared assignment authority + guard
body:
## Problem / why
Two sessions can claim the SAME backlog item -> double-claim. Observed: `wg work --epic BI-PF-0390` returned
`assigned: true` for BI-PF-0396 even though another session already held it. The claim should have FAILED.

## 5-Why (RCCA)
1. BI-PF-0396 was assigned to two sessions at once.
2. The lease lives in the backlog item file (`item.execution{}`, git-shared) BUT the other session's claim was only
   in THEIR working copy (not committed/pushed) -> invisible to my instance -> seen as free.
3. Each session runs its OWN PF API instance over a SEPARATE working copy -> two assignment authorities.
4. ADR-0003 assumes ONE PF (single assignment authority). Running N dev instances breaks that guarantee; the lease
   is only shared after a commit/push (racy).
5. No guard detects a second instance / foreign token / an uncoordinated (unpushed) lease.
ROOT CAUSE: multiple PF API instances = multiple assignment authorities; the per-item lease is not globally
coordinated at claim time (same class as BI-PF-0457, which fixed the ID counter with a git-CAS authority).

## Corrective (corrects the earlier per-session direction)
Make the dev model a SINGLE shared PF API instance (one authority) that ALL sessions use (shared URL + shared
token) -> one serializer of `execution{}` -> atomic claims. (Per-session APIs are WRONG here - they guarantee
double-claims.)

## Robust option
Coordinate the lease through a shared git-remote CAS authority (like `refs/heads/pf-id-counter` for ids), so
claims are atomic even with multiple instances/offline.

## Guard
- Refuse to start a second dev API on an already-owned port (detect a foreign PF instance).
- A claim that finds `execution.worker_id` set (even unpushed) fails closed.
- Optional: claim via the shared CAS/authority; verify the lease round-trips.

## Acceptance (G/W/T)
- Given two sessions and one item, when both `wg work`, then exactly ONE is assigned and the other fails closed.
- Given a second dev API on the same host, then it refuses (or the worker fails closed with a clear message).

## Related
ADR-0003 (PF = single assignment authority); BI-PF-0457 (id double-alloc - same class); IS-PF-0036 (one working tree).

decisions.note: Corrected direction: per-session dev APIs are WRONG (guarantee double-claims). Fix = ONE shared PF API instance (single assignment authority) all sessions use; optional git-CAS lease for cross-instance atomicity; guard against a second instance / uncoordinated lease.

brief.problem:
The local dev PF API is NOT session-scoped: `scripts/dev/dev_server.py` binds a FIXED port (8000) and the worker
defaults to a GLOBAL URL (`pf_api_url = http://127.0.0.1:8000`). With >1 session on the same host (allowed by
IS-PF-0036 as long as they use separate folders), each folder generates its OWN `data/local/dev-api-token`
(different tokens), but they all target port 8000 -> only one server binds; a worker in session B hits session
A's server -> token mismatch -> 401. (Observed: `wg work` 401 'invalid or missing bearer token' after another
session's API was on 8000.)
brief.what_adds: Defect/RCCA: dev API is not session-scoped (fixed port 8000 + global URL) -> concurrent sessions 401/collide; unique port + discovery file + guard
